blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Repair break-even matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: One bounded repair attempt beats immediate unwind-and-rebuild iff its measured success rate exceeds p* = C_repair / C_fallback, evaluated separately in time and dollars.

questions.q: The section **Exercises** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Reversibility is relative to a subsystem and a grant, so a plan is organized into compensable preparation, a single pivot, and owned follow-up duties, with every check that can precede the pivot hoisted ahead of it.
Scoped circuit breakers, a single retry owner, and bulkheads bound three different quantities when many trajectories share one dependency.

On suspicion, fail-safe defaults hold the trajectory at every dispatch boundary without the agent's cooperation while preregistered cleanup runs under a separate narrow grant until residual obligations settle.
